# Garry Kasparov
Garry Kasparov is a former world chess champion and a prominent political activist, best known for his rivalry with Anatoly Karpov and his eventual break with the FIDE World Chess Federation in 1993. Born in Baku to an Armenian mother and Jewish father, he fled pogroms in 1990 and became a central figure in the Russian opposition to Vladimir Putin. His political career includes founding the Democratic Party of Russia, leading the United Civil Front, and organizing major protests such as the "March of the Dissenters." He was designated a "foreign agent" in 2022, placed on Russia's "terrorists" list in 2024, and has called for the fall of Putin's regime, support for Ukraine's admission to NATO, and the dismantling of authoritarian structures in Russia and Iran.
Beyond politics, Kasparov is a prolific writer and chess analyst who authored the five-volume series *My Great Predecessors* and the book *Winter Is Coming* . He held the record for the highest Elo rating in history (2851) and spent 255 months ranked No. 1 globally. Following his retirement in 2005, he has remained active in chess through coaching, exhibitions, and media, including a notable match against Deep Blue in 1997. He also explored emerging technologies, promoting NFTs in 2021 and expressing cautious optimism regarding artificial intelligence. Kasparov has received numerous awards, including the Chess Oscar and the Morris B. Abram Human Rights Award, and maintains a significant online community through his platform, Kasparov Chess.
